chunks: From him, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Eat the slaughtered meat of the polytheists if you hear them mentioning the name of Allah over it, and do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Arab Christians.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the meat of polytheists and Arab Christians according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the juristic distinction between general polytheists and Arab Christians, a key topic in Shia fiqh regarding the criteria for 'Ahl al-Kitab' status. While the meat of polytheists is permitted upon hearing the invocation of Allah's name, Arab Christians are excluded from this permissibility, reflecting their specific historical and theological context. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the actual recitation and audibility of the Bismillah during slaughter to validate the act.
